In one sentence: an occupational description of support work around airport field inspection, operational information, safety procedures, and recordkeeping; the specific work and authority depend on the country, employer, and position.

The tasks of airfield operations specialists fall into four categories: movement-area inspection and safety procedures (inspecting movement-area field and facility conditions according to regulations and operations manuals, implementing airport safety procedures to ensure a safe environment for personnel and aircraft operations, inspecting airport property and perimeters to maintain controlled access, coordinating runway and taxiway snow removal, managing wildlife on and around airport fields, and planning and coordinating airport construction); operations coordination and information publication (coordinating communications between air traffic control and maintenance personnel, using landing and navigation aids and digital terminal communication equipment to perform tasks, receiving, transmitting, and controlling messages, receiving and publishing weather and flight plan data, publishing notices to inform crews of airport status, and relaying departures, arrivals, delays, and airport status to superior control agencies); flight and crew support (monitoring the arrival, parking, refueling, loading, and departure of all aircraft, providing crews with the information and services needed for airport management and flight planning, coordinating crew accommodation, catering, refueling, ground transportation, and transit maintenance needs, conducting departure and arrival briefings, coordinating flight itinerary changes with the corresponding air traffic control agencies, checking military flight plans with civil agencies, and monitoring and managing drone operations within airport airspace); and recordkeeping and coordination (maintaining flight and incident logs, crew flight records, and arrival/departure operations records, posting visual display and status boards, training operations personnel, and assisting in responding to aircraft and medical emergencies). This is the U.S. O*NET task set, comprising core, supplemental, and new tasks, and does not mean all positions must perform them; in China, responsibilities must be confirmed separately for positions such as operations command and airfield maintenance.

O*NET 53-2022.00 Airfield Operations Specialists: ensure the safe takeoff and landing of commercial and military aircraft; responsibilities include coordination between air traffic control and maintenance personnel, dispatch, use of airport landing and navigation aids, implementation of airport safety procedures, monitoring and maintenance of flight records, and application of weather information knowledge. Common job titles include Airfield Operations Specialist, Airport Operations Agent, Airport Operations Coordinator, Airport Operations Officer, Flight Follower, Operations Agent, Operations Coordinator, Operations Officer, and Operations Specialist.

entries: Movement-area inspection | field and facilities | conduct daily comprehensive inspections and periodic walk-throughs of runways, taxiways, aprons, and runway strips according to regulations and operations manuals; check surfaces, markings, lighting, and drainage; and record defects and take or report corrective action.

Safety procedures and access | controlled access | implement airport safety procedures, inspect airport property and perimeters to maintain controlled access, and manage personnel and vehicle permits for entering the movement area.

Operations coordination | control and maintenance | coordinate communications between air traffic control and maintenance personnel, coordinate with agencies to support airport management activities, and manage runway and taxiway snow-removal coordination.

Information relay | weather and plans | U.S. O*NET supplemental/new tasks include messages, weather, flight plans, and airport status information. Actual receipt, relay, or publication must follow position authority; the Chinese side does not grant notice-signing authority on this basis, which is handled by authorized agencies, and operations positions verify source data and status according to the division of labor.

Flight and crew support | coordination and briefing | U.S. O*NET supplemental/new tasks include arrival, parking, refueling, loading, and departure coordination and crew information briefings. Specific weather, plan, dispatch, and notice work is handled according to jurisdiction and position authority; the operations position title does not confer dispatch or publication qualification.

Recordkeeping and emergency response | logs and response | maintain flight and incident logs, crew flight records, and operations records; post status boards; train operations personnel; and assist in responding to aircraft and medical emergencies.

entries.answer: The tasks of airfield operations specialists fall into four categories: movement-area inspection and safety procedures (inspecting movement-area field and facility conditions according to regulations and operations manuals, implementing airport safety procedures to ensure a safe environment for personnel and aircraft operations, inspecting airport property and perimeters to maintain controlled access, coordinating runway and taxiway snow removal, managing wildlife on and around airport fields, and planning and coordinating airport construction); operations coordination and information publication (coordinating communications between air traffic control and maintenance personnel, using landing and navigation aids and digital terminal communication equipment to perform tasks, receiving, transmitting, and controlling messages, receiving and publishing weather and flight plan data, publishing notices to inform crews of airport status, and relaying departures, arrivals, delays, and airport status to superior control agencies); flight and crew support (monitoring the arrival, parking, refueling, loading, and departure of all aircraft, providing crews with the information and services needed for airport management and flight planning, coordinating crew accommodation, catering, refueling, ground transportation, and transit maintenance needs, conducting departure and arrival briefings, coordinating flight itinerary changes with the corresponding air traffic control agencies, checking military flight plans with civil agencies, and monitoring and managing drone operations within airport airspace); and recordkeeping and coordination (maintaining flight and incident logs, crew flight records, and arrival/departure operations records, posting visual display and status boards, training operations personnel, and assisting in responding to aircraft and medical emergencies). This is the U.S. O*NET task set, comprising core, supplemental, and new tasks, and does not mean all positions must perform them; in China, responsibilities must be confirmed separately for positions such as operations command and airfield maintenance.
